result.title: Context-Aware Topological Distillation Graph Network for Asymmetric EEG-Eye Movement Emotion Recognition
result.summary: EEG-eye movement emotion recognition can support mental-health monitoring and adaptive interfaces, but most fusion models treat the two signals as parallel features, classify each window alone and degrade when eye data are lost. We propose the Context-Aware Topological Distillation Graph Network (CTD-GNet), in which EEG features form the nodes of an electrode graph, and eye movements and preceding windows modulate its edges, nodes and readout, the edges through electrode-specific prompts. Bidirectional distillation of the graph, node relations and predictions couples this multimodal teacher with a single-window EEG student, improving the teacher and aligning the two graphs 35-fold. In leave-one-subject-out tests on SEED and SEED-IV against 17 baselines, CTD-GNet has the highest mean accuracy, 84.91% and 76.17%, significantly above 9 and 6 of 13 eye-based baselines after Holm correction, the smallest cross-subject spread among multimodal models and the highest worst-subject accuracy. It is the most accurate model at every rate of missing eye data on SEED-IV, keeps 66.1% on SEED without eye data, more than any EEG-only model, and stays 9.3 and 11.9 points above all single-window fusion models under eye-movement noise of one standard deviation. On film clips unseen in training, it leads on SEED with 77.1%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CTD-GNet：以脑电特征作为电极图节点，用眼动与前后窗口通过电极级 prompt 调制图的边、节点和读出，并通过图、节点关系与预测的双向蒸馏把多模态教师与单窗口 EEG 学生对齐，在 SEED/SEED-IV 的留一被试测试中验证眼动缺失与噪声下的稳健性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其跨模态双向蒸馏在眼动数据缺失时仍维持性能，可能为 LVR 中「视觉证据被旁路或信息坍缩时，如何用训练监督把多模态信息压入单一推理状态」提供可供核查的线索，但任务与评价体系差异较大，需较多核查。
